div.head: Had 4
div.ab: And to hadbote, gif fulbrice wyrðe, toeacan þam rihtwere, æt þam þriddan stæpe þreo pund to bote mid godcundan scrifte.
⁊ to hádbote, gif fulbrice wurðe, toeacan þam rihtwere, æt þam þriddan stæpe þreo pund to bóte mid godcundan scrifte.
⁊ to hadbote, gif fullbryce wurðe, toeacan þam rihtwere, æt þam þryddan stæpe III pund to bote mid godcundan scrifte.
Et ad emendacionem ordinis, si plena fiat fractura, supra rectam weram, in tercio gradu tres libre emendentur cum digna penitentia.
And to hadbote, gif fullbryce wurðe, toeacan þam rihtwere æt þam þryddan stæpe III pund to bote mid godcundan scrifte.

Und wenn vollständige [tödtliche] Verletzung [eines Klerikers] eintritt, [zahle Verletzer] ausser dessen gesetzlichem Wergeld, bei dem dritten Ordo als Klerusbusse 3 Pfund zur Busse, neben geistlicher Poenitenz.
And if full [fatal] injury [to a cleric] occurs, [let the offender pay], besides his lawful wergild, for the third grade 3 pounds as compensation for orders, with spiritual penance.

And as compensation for one in orders if a full breach of the peace occurs, the perpetrator must make amends for the third rank by paying three pounds as a penalty in addition to the standard wergild and by doing spiritual penance.

And in compensation for [an offence against a man in] orders, if a full breach occurs, one must pay for the third degree with three pounds in addition to the legal wergild, and intercede zealously with ecclesiastical penance.
div.note: U: not in Whitelock’s English Historical Documents, which prints only Had 1–2 and 9–11 (with “…” for the rest); the source of this translation is not recorded.
full breach of the peace: Equivalent to the “loss of life” specified in the previous clause.
